codes.repair: Check that the code under test sends the message to the test's process (`self()`) and that the pattern matches its exact shape, or give a slow sender more time with `assert_receive PATTERN, TIMEOUT_MS`.

codes.name: test-panicked
codes.title: test failed in the runtime
codes.summary: A test, or the test program running it, failed in a way that is not a Mesh panic or a failed assertion: the runtime panicked, or the program was killed by a signal or exited without reporting a failure.
codes.repair: Read the runtime's report above this diagnostic. Report it with the test that reproduces it; if the program was killed, check the memory and resource limits it ran under.

codes.name: no-tests
codes.title: no tests found
codes.summary: `meshc test` found no `*.test.mpl` file at its target.
codes.repair: Run `meshc test` from the project root or pass it the directory or `*.test.mpl` file that holds the tests, and name test files `<name>.test.mpl`.

codes.name: law-falsified
codes.title: law falsified
codes.summary: Verification found inputs for which the implementation and law disagree.
codes.repair: Reproduce the counterexample in the note and fix the implementation or correct the stated law.

codes.name: law-unverified
codes.title: law unverified
codes.summary: Verification could not establish a verdict for the law inventory.
codes.repair: Read the reason and resolve the reported obligation before treating the law as verified.

codes.name: law-unsupported
codes.title: law unsupported
codes.summary: The verifier cannot model the law or a construct that it depends on.
codes.repair: Rewrite the marked expression using the supported verification fragment.

codes.name: law-binding-unresolved
codes.title: law binding unresolved
codes.summary: A law, import, or proof could not be bound to a unique declaration.
codes.repair: Check the law name and its target import, including the module, visibility, and number of parameters.

codes.name: law-signature-mismatch
codes.title: law signature mismatch
codes.summary: The law does not declare the same concrete function signature as its target.
codes.repair: Match the target parameter and return types in the law declaration.

codes.name: solver-missing
codes.title: required Z3 solver unavailable
codes.summary: Verification could not use the required Z3 4.15.7 solver.
codes.repair: Install Z3 4.15.7 and put it on `PATH` or set `MESH_VERIFY_Z3` to its executable.

codes.name: prover-missing
codes.title: required Lean toolchain unavailable
codes.summary: Verification could not use the required Lean 4.36.0 toolchain.
codes.repair: Install Lean 4.36.0 and set `MESH_VERIFY_LEAN` to the trusted Lean executable. For `--verdict`, install the replay tools in the toolchain as well.

codes.name: solver-timeout
codes.title: verification time budget exhausted
codes.summary: A verification tool did not finish within the time budget.
codes.repair: Simplify the obligation or increase `MESH_VERIFY_TIMEOUT_MS` in milliseconds and retry.

codes.name: proof-rejected
codes.title: proof rejected
codes.summary: A proof checker or proof scenario failed.
codes.repair: Read the checker or scenario failure and correct the proof or the condition it checks.

codes.name: proof-replay-mismatch
codes.title: proof replay mismatch
codes.summary: The independent replay failed to confirm the exported proof.
codes.repair: Inspect the export and independent checker output, fix the proof or replay toolchain, and rerun `meshc verify --verdict`.

codes.name: redundant-arm
codes.title: redundant match arm
codes.summary: A match arm can never run, because earlier arms already match every value it would.
codes.repair: Remove the arm, or move it before the arm that covers it.

example.bad:
fn main() do
  let n = case 1 do
    _ -> 0
    1 -> 2
  end
  println("#{n}")
end
example.fixed:
fn main() do
  let n = case 1 do
    1 -> 2
    _ -> 0
  end
  println("#{n}")
end

codes.name: non-first-clause-annotation
codes.title: annotation on a later clause is ignored
codes.summary: Visibility, type parameters, or a return type are written on a clause other than the first of a multi-clause function, where they have no effect.
codes.repair: Write the annotation on the first clause only, and remove it from the later ones.

example.bad:
fn label(0) -> String = "zero"
fn label(n) -> String = "other"

fn main() do
  println(label(0))
end
example.fixed:
fn label(0) -> String = "zero"
fn label(n) = "other"

fn main() do
  println(label(0))
end

codes.name: non-exhaustive-clauses
codes.title: function clauses do not cover every argument
codes.summary: A multi-clause function or closure has no clause for some arguments, and a call with one of them panics at run time.
codes.repair: Add a clause for each missing pattern, or a final catch-all clause.

example.bad:
fn label(0) = "zero"
fn label(1) = "one"

fn main() do
  println(label(0))
end
example.fixed:
fn label(0) = "zero"
fn label(n) = "other"

fn main() do
  println(label(0))
end

codes.name: invalid-arguments
codes.title: invalid command arguments
codes.summary: An option, value, or combination of arguments is invalid.
codes.repair: Run the command with `--help` and correct the invocation.

codes.name: path-not-found
codes.title: path unavailable
codes.summary: A command could not access the input or output path it needs.
codes.repair: Check the path and its permissions. For output, use a writable directory.

codes.name: unknown-guide-topic
codes.title: unknown guide topic
codes.summary: The embedded guide has no reference with this name.
codes.repair: Run `meshc guide` to list topics.

codes.name: unknown-diagnostic-code
codes.title: unknown diagnostic code
codes.summary: The catalog does not recognize the requested code or name.
codes.repair: Run `meshc explain` to list diagnostic codes.

codes.name: skills-install-conflict
codes.title: skill installation conflict
codes.summary: An existing skill or installation receipt prevents Mesh from updating the skill safely.
codes.repair: Inspect the existing destination. Move it aside if you want Mesh to manage that location, then retry setup.

codes.name: skills-setup-needs-target
codes.title: non-interactive setup requires a target
codes.summary: Skill setup requires explicit approval and a coding tool when it cannot prompt.
codes.repair: Run `meshc skills setup --yes --target <agent>`. Run `meshc skills setup --help` to list agents.

codes.name: would-reformat
codes.title: file would be reformatted
codes.summary: The file differs from the formatter output.
codes.repair: Run `meshc fmt <path>` to format the file.

codes.name: update-failed
codes.title: toolchain update failed
codes.summary: The updater could not download or run the canonical installer.
codes.repair: Correct the failing installer step named in the message and rerun the update.

codes.name: registry-unreachable
codes.title: registry request failed
codes.summary: A transport or server failure prevented the registry request from completing.
codes.repair: Check the registry URL, network connection, and registry availability, then retry.

codes.name: registry-auth-failed
codes.title: registry authentication failed
codes.summary: The command could not obtain a token with access to the registry operation.
codes.repair: Run `meshpkg login` with a valid token that has permission for the operation.

codes.name: publish-conflict
codes.title: package version already published
codes.summary: The registry already has the package version being published.
codes.repair: Increase the package version in `mesh.toml` and publish the new version.

codes.name: registry-response-invalid
codes.title: registry response invalid
codes.summary: The registry returned an unexpected status, invalid data, or a package that did not match its checksum.
codes.repair: Check the package name, version, and registry URL. Report invalid metadata or checksum mismatches to the registry operator.

codes.name: cluster-command-failed
codes.title: cluster command failed
codes.summary: A cluster operator request could not complete.
codes.repair: Check the target node and operator configuration named in the error before retrying.

codes.name: migration-failed
codes.title: migration failed
codes.summary: A database migration command could not complete.
codes.repair: Fix the reported migration or database connection failure, then check migration status before retrying.

codes.name: plaintext-report-changed
codes.title: plaintext report changed
codes.summary: The current report differs from the committed plaintext report.
codes.repair: Review the changes, then regenerate the committed report with `meshc plaintext-report --output <path>`.
